Since 221 = 13·17 and 403 = 13·31, gcd(221, 403) = 13.

Build a bipartite graph with apples on one side and students on the other, and join an apple to a student whenever that student receives a piece of that apple. The number of pieces equals the number of edges. Each connected component must have its apples and students in the right proportion, so a component with a apples and s students needs a/s = 221/403 = 17/31. Every component therefore contains at least 17 apples and 31 students, and there are at most 221/17 = 13 components.

A connected graph on V vertices has at least V − 1 edges. So the number of pieces is at least (221 + 403) − (number of components) ≥ 624 − 13 = 611.

This bound can be reached. Split the students into 13 groups of 31 and the apples into 13 groups of 17. For each group, 17 apples among 31 students can be shared with 17 + 31 − 1 = 47 pieces, by cutting the apples in sequence, each apple into the pieces handed to successive students, so that the graph forms a path. This gives 13 · 47 = 611 pieces.

ANSWER: 611
